body.x: As GPU power density climbs, air cooling alone struggles to remove the heat that high-density AI servers produce, and the power and water used for cooling become an environmental issue of their own. Immersion cooling, in which entire servers sit in tanks of dielectric fluid, can handle the heat but calls for large volumes of fluid, heavy tanks and reinforced floors.

CENS Co., Ltd., a climate tech company in Sujeong-gu, Seongnam, Gyeonggi Province, is pursuing a third approach. The company's name stands for "Cooling & Energy New Solutions," and its CEO is Juye Lee. CENS was selected as a winner in the FIX 2026 Innovation Awards and says it plans to use the award's benefits to promote its technology and meet buyers.

CENS says it manages the heat of high-temperature industrial equipment, such as AI data centers and eco-friendly ships, with liquid cooling. It built its expertise on water-cooling power conversion equipment for eco-friendly vessels and then moved into liquid cooling for AI data centers. Its current focus is CENS-D, a rack-scale precision spray cooling platform. Unlike full immersion, the company says, CENS-D supplies dielectric coolant directly to components where heat is concentrated, such as GPUs and CPUs, which it says cools high-density servers while greatly reducing coolant use and structural floor load. Lee is described in the application as a "sustainable infrastructure architect" mastering the heat and water constraints of high-density power facilities with precision liquid cooling.

According to CENS, the system uniformly sprays a non-conductive dielectric coolant across the whole server rack chamber and adds a targeted spray on key heat sources, with nozzle configurations tuned to the supported server platforms. The company reports that this reduces dielectric coolant use by up to 95% and structural load by 70% compared with full immersion. A proprietary AI-based thermal design power (TDP) tracking algorithm adjusts coolant flow to real-time computing workloads, which CENS says removes unnecessary pumping energy. An integrated cooling distribution unit (CDU) inside the rack combines pumping, heat exchange, filtering, circulation and monitoring in one closed-loop module, and the company lists 1+1 redundant hardware, automatic failover within 10 seconds and a leak-free maintenance design for reliability. It says the system achieves Zero water usage effectiveness (WUE) and can recover waste heat for uses such as district heating.

The company positions CENS-D for retrofits. It says the lightweight rack-scale design lets existing air-cooled data centers move to high-density AI use without large-scale reconstruction, reducing deployment complexity, construction costs, lead times and downtime. It says it is designed to work with global Tier-1 server manufacturers so that thermal management can be built into AI servers at the factory. CENS names three main customer groups: colocation and enterprise data center operators pursuing AI retrofits of air-cooled facilities; global hyperscale cloud providers facing strict environmental, social and governance (ESG) and water rules, for which it cites Zero WUE and a power usage effectiveness (PUE) of 1.1; and Tier-1 server manufacturers, which it calls its strategic core target.

Its track record is mainly domestic. CENS says it set up an in-house corporate R&D center and won cooling design contracts for industrial high-voltage facilities, then launched CENS-P, a water-cooling solution for next-generation marine power conversion systems (PCS). In 2025, it was registered as an official vendor for two major conglomerates and delivered marine variable frequency drive (VFD) water-cooling systems. It says it has completed development and core performance verification of CENS-D and signed nondisclosure agreements with leading global Tier-1 server manufacturers and several data center infrastructure partners. It has been selected for government R&D programs in deep-tech and climate-tech, received seed investment from Korea Investment Accelerator and won TIPS R&D funding.

The company states two purposes for the exhibition. One is to validate its technology publicly and promote it through the award's press coverage, on-site media connections and award-winning content promotion. The other is to use the award's domestic and international buyer matching and Plug and Play support to start technical partnership and adoption discussions with data center operators, colocation providers and server makers.

CENS has no direct overseas exports. It says it has focused on commercialization and operating references at large domestic industrial sites first, and that it has signed nondisclosure agreements and is discussing technical integration with leading global Tier-1 server manufacturers and a domestic data center operator. Its primary target is the U.S., specifically North American hyperscalers, Tier-1 server OEMs and large colocation operators. The company calls the U.S. the home of technology and the market with the highest demand for advanced thermal management, and says it wants to prove its competitiveness there on technical merit. It acknowledges that data center and high-voltage power facility markets are conservative, with strict reliability requirements, and that its biggest bottleneck is breaking into a market dominated by global Big Tech and established infrastructure companies. It plans to build references and run PoCs with key local partners.

CENS describes a three-phase roadmap: commercializing CENS-D and securing core references in AI data center liquid cooling; expanding into the retrofit market for existing air-cooled data centers; and extending the technology to high-heat industrial uses including energy storage systems (ESS), eco-friendly ships and power conversion systems. The company says its ultimate goal is to become a global circular thermal energy platform company that manages equipment heat and recycles waste heat into usable energy.

FIX 2026 is the third edition of a future-industry exhibition that brings together and links innovative technologies in future mobility, robotics, AI and ICT, and startups. It will run from Wednesday, Oct. 21, to Saturday, Oct. 24, at EXCO in Daegu. Under the theme "AI, Beyond Tech into Reality," it offers AI-based technology exhibitions, conferences and lectures by experts from Korea and abroad, and networking programs that share industry trends and core technologies.
